name: Men's Corporate Service Dress: navy blazer, white shirt and tie, gray trousers (blank nametag)
size_basis: Silhouette traced from images/base/male_semi_formal.webp (581x719 px) at 0.0474 in/px, which makes the sleeve-to-sleeve 25.12 in (a men's 40R; the Class A coat at its true scale, make-blues-a.js, is 25.27 in). Trousers are added below the base image's cropped hem. No real garment was measured. Checked against CAPR 39-1 Fig 4.14 (PDF page 87 at 8x) with the figure's 1398 px sleeve-to-sleeve taken as the sheet's 25.12 in (55.6 px/in): the figure's crest centre is 5.53 in from the centre line (Fig 4.12, page 84: 5.37 in), the sheet's pocket and crest centre are 5.49 in from it; the sheet's silhouette, pocket top (12.38 in), crest and lapel overlaid on Fig 4.14 agree within 0.1 in. The lapel is the figure's: its peak is 5.58 in from the centre line at y 6.1 in, the lapel 3.9 in wide, its outer edge 5.35 / 4.44 / 3.97 / 2.84 in from the centre line at y 7.3 / 9.4 / 10.4 / 12.4 in. A rack of 4 miniatures at 11/16 in (2.75 in wide) centred on the pocket has its inner edge 4.12 in from the centre line, so the lapel edge crosses its top rows (1.23 in over the rack at y 7.3, 0.32 in at y 9.4) and clears it from y 10.4 down; Fig 4.12 draws the rack the same way, its top rows against the lapel edge. Moving the pocket out or narrowing the lapel enough to clear the top rows would leave Figs 4.12 and 4.14 (see DECISIONS.md DORAN5-ART-2).
landmarks_note: rects are {x,y,w,h}; polygons and polylines are [[x,y]...]; all in user units (0.01 in), origin top-left of the artwork box. lapel_left / lapel_right: the lapel-foreground faces (wearer's left is +x); arm_seam_left / arm_seam_right: the armhole seam from the shoulder point down to the chest; shoulder_left / shoulder_right: the top edge of the shoulder from the neck to the sleeve head
documented: navy single-breasted blazer, two or three buttons, notched lapels, two front flap pockets and a left breast pocket (CAPR 39-1 4.2.3.1)
CAP Crest sewn to the centre of the left breast pocket or in the same relative position (4.2.3.1.1.1)
nametag slot: top edge aligned with top edge of the left breast pocket (4.2.3.1.1.2); the plate itself is a separate asset (assets/nameplates)
chaplain badge mandatory, 1/2 inch above the nametag (4.2.3.1.1.3)
white shirt; tie mandatory with this combination (4.2.3.2, 4.2.3.4)
assumed: tie #1b3f8f (edge #0a2260): the AF blue tie of the aviator shirt sheets (CAPR 39-1 4.2.3.4 allows the CAP regimental or the AF blue tie; one tie is worn, so the blazer figure and the aviator shirt beside it show the same tie); the blazer photo tie sampled darker navy #0d2a66 (review FIX-ART-r2 item 6)

trouser gray #736f6c: the same medium gray as the aviator-shirt sheets (CAPR 39-1 4.2.3.3 and 4.2.5.1.5 name one medium gray, solid colour); the blazer photo sampled #8a8d95, a bluer and lighter tone that read as a different trouser beside the aviator companion (review FIX-ART-r1 item 8)
nametag slot size 3.375 x 0.9 in (width from the CAP cadet plate; 3.75:1 proportion read from CAPR 39-1 Fig A6-3; the blazer plate is not dimensioned)
CAP Crest art is a simplified parametric redraw
collar/tie/shirt geometry read off the base image
trousers added below the cropped blazer hem
colours sampled from the base image / figure
